task: Explain the documented historical 袁 to 元 substitution briefly, distinguishing a component substitution from whole-word borrowing. State a proposed sound basis only as supported by the actual evidence; do not conflate 袁 pictured-object uncertainty with an independently attested component-reading comparison.

findings: `learner.components[1].text` should explain the graphic change: 袁 is the sound element in traditional 遠, while an existing variant substituted 元 for 袁 before 远 became the standardized simplified form. The current wording only says 袁 is not visible, obscuring that supported change (E9, X-80175cb4c660d0e4c836, X-18e73dc061123e0763a9).

Revise `learner.overview` to explain that the variant’s 元 substitution was proposed because the old and new words sounded similar, while qualifying that 袁’s original referent and pronunciation are unsettled. The current overview names the substitution but leaves the borrowing mechanism unexplained. Cite `X-80175cb4c660d0e4c836`, `X-18e73dc061123e0763a9`, `X-ecdabe87f5904b8e3aef`, and `X-9ae0a097668adca7aae7`.
